# ORBIT YEAR — program and science facts

## Program identity

- Institution: Meridian City Planetarium
- Program: ORBIT YEAR
- Invitation: Find the pattern. Ask the next question.
- Invitation status: optional copy
- Year: 2027
- Calendar type: quarterly learning periods
- Institution symbol: planetarium-mark.png
- Institution symbol color: #18324A

## Program records

| Code | Exact theme title | Program period | Learning question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | The changing Moon | January–March 2027 | Why does the visible bright shape change? |
| Q2 | When shadows align | April–June 2027 | What is different about a solar and a lunar eclipse? |
| Q3 | One tilt, two seasons | July–September 2027 | Why do northern and southern seasons differ? |
| Q4 | A ruler for space | October–December 2027 | How can one unit describe very large distances? |

## Text records

- Theme poster and digital adaptation program block: ORBIT YEAR; Meridian City Planetarium; corresponding exact theme title; corresponding program period
- Name and title typography: original words; flexible capitalization and line breaks
- Period typography: original periods; unambiguous equivalent date typography
- Learning questions and explanations: original meaning; flexible phrasing
- Standalone science diagram text: corresponding theme title and science labels
- Rules board program text: ORBIT YEAR
- Schematic label: Schematic — not to scale
- Linear ruler label: Distance scale in AU; body symbols not to scale

## Q1 science records

- Theme: The changing Moon
- Moonlight source: reflected sunlight
- Ordinary phase model: one half of the Moon illuminated by the Sun
- Phase mechanism: changing fraction of the illuminated half visible from Earth as the Moon orbits
- Phase cycle: about 29.5 days
- Appearance viewpoint: Earth observer
- Light-side orientation convention: Northern Hemisphere
- New Moon symbol option: labelled outline

| Sequence | Phase |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | new Moon |
| 2 | waxing crescent |
| 3 | first quarter |
| 4 | waxing gibbous |
| 5 | full Moon |
| 6 | waning gibbous |
| 7 | last quarter |
| 8 | waning crescent |

## Q2 science records

- Theme: When shadows align
- Solar eclipse order: Sun–Moon–Earth
- Solar eclipse shadow: Moon's shadow reaches part of Earth
- Lunar eclipse order: Sun–Earth–Moon
- Lunar eclipse shadow: Earth's shadow reaches the Moon
- Orbital relationship: Moon's orbital plane tilted relative to Earth's orbital plane
- Eclipse frequency explanation: eclipse alignment occurs only when orbital position and the tilted orbital planes permit it
- Body labels: Sun; Earth; Moon
- Comparison labels: solar eclipse; lunar eclipse

## Q3 science records

- Theme: One tilt, two seasons
- Axial direction: approximately constant through one Earth orbit
- Summer mechanism: hemisphere tilted toward the Sun receives more direct sunlight
- Opposite hemisphere: winter
- Opposite-season explanation: axial tilt and sunlight angle

| Orbital configuration | Northern Hemisphere | Southern Hemisphere |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Around June | summer | winter |
| Around December | winter | summer |

## Q4 science records

- Theme: A ruler for space
- Unit: astronomical unit, AU
- AU definition for this program: approximately the mean Earth–Sun distance
- Rounded AU value: about 150 million kilometres
- Distance quantity: mean orbital distance from the Sun
- Ruler geometry: one linear distance scale
- Body symbols: independent of the distance scale

| Body | Ruler position in AU | Record meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sun | 0 | Distance origin |
| Earth | 1 | Rounded mean orbital distance from the Sun |
| Saturn | 9.5 | Rounded mean orbital distance from the Sun |

## Representation records

- Schematic geometry: exaggerated body size, compressed distance or other explanatory spatial arrangement
- Schematic disclosure: Schematic — not to scale
- Linear AU ruler disclosure: Distance scale in AU; body symbols not to scale
- Embedded diagrams: same scale disclosure as their standalone equivalents
- Paired phenomena and hemispheres: explicit written labels supported by symbols and color
- Poster and digital teaching content: learning question, causal explanation and explanatory graphic
- Decorative star fields: atmospheric imagery
- Scientific image type: explanatory diagrams

## Carrier geometry

| Carrier | Geometry | Protected area |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theme poster | A1 portrait; 594 × 841 mm trim | 3 mm bleed; minimum 5 mm internal safe margin |
| Landscape screen | 16:9 | 5% inset from each edge |
| Social post | 1:1 | 5% inset from each edge |
| Animation | 16:9; 10 seconds | 5% inset from each edge |

## Source records

- Science source date: 10 September 2026
- Source text form: paraphrased science summaries

steps.userMessage:
ORBIT YEAR | A year of astronomy in public view

Meridian City Planetarium is commissioning the posters and digital graphics for ORBIT YEAR, our 2027 public learning program. The four themes are The changing Moon, January–March 2027; When shadows align, April–June 2027; One tilt, two seasons, July–September 2027; and A ruler for space, October–December 2027. These are quarterly learning periods. Build the series around the supplied institution mark and its color #18324A, with a shared explanation hierarchy and a distinct visual treatment for each theme. Every theme poster and digital adaptation carries "ORBIT YEAR", Meridian City Planetarium, its theme title and its program period. The invitation "Find the pattern. Ask the next question." is available as optional copy. Posters are A1, 594 × 841 mm, with 3 mm bleed and a minimum 5 mm internal safe margin. Digital applications use a landscape screen and square social posts, each with a 5% safe inset on every edge.

Scientific relationships are the backbone of the series. Moonlight is reflected sunlight; the changing view of the illuminated half produces a phase cycle of about 29.5 days. Eclipse graphics distinguish the Moon's shadow reaching Earth from Earth's shadow reaching the Moon, and explain why the tilted lunar orbit makes eclipses occasional. Seasonal graphics pair northern and southern conditions around June and December while preserving Earth's axial direction. The distance comparison uses approximately 150 million kilometres per AU, with the Sun at 0, Earth at 1 and Saturn at 9.5 on a linear ruler. Exaggerated explanatory geometry carries "Schematic — not to scale"; the ruler carries "Distance scale in AU; body symbols not to scale". These labels also accompany diagrams embedded in posters and digital artwork.

Audience: members of the public, teenagers and accompanying adults will use the series to understand basic astronomy, while the planetarium's education and communications teams will use the work to approve the year's public campaign.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the program records, learning questions, science summaries and representation conventions. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. carrier-geometry.png records the poster trim, bleed and safe margin alongside the screen and social safe areas. distance-relationship.png records the linear relationship between 0, 1 and 9.5 AU. planetarium-mark.png supplies the institution's existing symbol and color. visitor-corridor.png supplies the reading atmosphere of the corridor and outdoor lightboxes.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page information hierarchy specification, the starting document for the series, recording information priorities, placement by carrier, font families, weights and minimum sizes, A1 dimensions and margins, #18324A, and both scale labels
2. One series graphic rules board translating the specification into a master visual, four theme identifiers, typography, diagram symbols and caption treatments, with ORBIT YEAR, the A1 dimensions, #18324A and both scale labels printed on the board
3. Four A1 theme posters, one for each quarterly theme, each with its learning question, causal explanation and explanatory graphic
4. Two standalone science diagrams: one paired solar and lunar eclipse comparison for When shadows align, and one linear AU ruler for A ruler for space
5. Two landscape screen adaptations, one for The changing Moon and one for When shadows align, retaining each poster's program block, learning question, explanation and scientific relationship
6. Two square social posts, one for One tilt, two seasons and one for A ruler for space, retaining each poster's program block, learning question, explanation and scientific relationship
7. One 10-second animation of the When shadows align screen, with the program block visible throughout, the solar example in the opening frame and the lunar example in the closing frame, using the screen's wording and labels
8. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, reusing the specification, rules board, four posters, two diagrams, four digital adaptations and animation frames, with an application map locating the fixed facts

Acceptance:
- The specification establishes the hierarchy before the rules board and applications. The rules board and presentation repeat its A1 dimensions of 594 × 841 mm, color code #18324A and both exact scale labels; the four posters use its 3 mm bleed and minimum 5 mm internal safe margin.
- The four posters, four digital adaptations and animation pair ORBIT YEAR and Meridian City Planetarium with the correct theme title and quarterly period stated above. The institution symbol retains the geometry of planetarium-mark.png and #18324A across those nine applications.
- The changing Moon poster and screen explain reflected sunlight and the changing visible fraction of the illuminated half, state about 29.5 days, and show all eight phases from new Moon through waning crescent in the supplied order. Their phase appearances identify an Earth-observer view and the Northern Hemisphere convention.
- The When shadows align poster, screen, standalone diagram and animation label Sun, Earth and Moon; pair solar eclipse with Sun–Moon–Earth and lunar eclipse with Sun–Earth–Moon; and explain the tilted lunar orbit. The One tilt, two seasons poster and social post show a consistent axial direction, pairing northern summer with southern winter around June and northern winter with southern summer around December.
- The A ruler for space poster, social post and standalone diagram state about 150 million kilometres per AU and place Sun, Earth and Saturn at 0, 1 and 9.5 on one linear distance scale. Each carries the exact distance-scale label. Every schematic explanation in the posters, diagrams, digital adaptations and animation carries the exact schematic label, with written labels distinguishing paired phenomena and hemispheres.
- The two screen adaptations, two social posts and animation place copy and the institution mark within the 5% safe inset. The animation lasts 10 seconds and matches the specified opening and closing examples. The presentation contains at least 8 pages and maps each program record, scientific relationship and scale label to its named applications.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
